name: Swiss French (Romandy)
notes: Swiss French as a thin variant of Metropolitan French (fr-FR). Two features are stated, from the PFC survey of Neuchâtel (PFC page, d) 1) and 4)): patte ≠ pâte is kept as a difference of LENGTH ('opposition de longueur: Suisse : Neuchâtel'), so ⟨â⟩ is [ɑː]; and faites [fɛt] ≠ fête [fɛːt] and belle ≠ bêle are kept by length, so ⟨ê⟩ is [ɛː]. At Nyon the same pâte contrast is one of timbre, and [ɑː] keeps that timbre. The /ɛ̃/ ~ /œ̃/ contrast (brin ≠ brun) is kept as in fr-FR. The PFC page notes that it is being neutralised among young speakers at Neuchâtel and kept at Nyon. NOT MODELLED: the length opposition in nu ~ nue and vit ~ vie (a vowel before a mute ⟨e⟩; the page gives four pairs, not a rule), vowel length elsewhere, vowel quality, the diphthongisation of final /eː/, and the numerals septante, huitante and nonante (numbers are out of scope). The page is a survey summary at two points and not a description of every Swiss variety.

sources.author: Projet PFC (Phonologie du français contemporain), FLORAL-PFC
sources.title: Le français expliqué: Prononciation, I. Le système vocalique, d) Variation
sources.notes: READ (open web page; the page metadata gives 2010 as its publication year and 2017 as its last change). The page reports, from PFC survey points: patte ≠ pâte by LENGTH at Neuchâtel (Switzerland) and Tournai (Belgium) and by timbre at Nyon; patte = pâte at Brunoy and Abidjan; brin ≠ brun kept at Tournai and Nyon (very slight timbre difference), at Toulouse and Abidjan (marked), and fading among young speakers at Neuchâtel; the length opposition faites [fɛt] ~ fête [fɛːt], belle ~ bêle, nu ~ nue, vit ~ vie at Neuchâtel. The page cites Gadet (1996) and Léon (2007).

ancestors.notes: Standard Metropolitan French, the base of every other variety here.
